doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Soprano out of favor; coming up on Bird
summary: Old sopranos were given away; Jordan skipped Bechet's generation and came up listening to Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: That’s a great story. Like you realized that you were not going to be able to stay away from that saxophone so you had to handicap it.
Exactly. That’s exactly what I had to do.
That’s funny. It’s interesting, you said you were hearing high. Did it occur to you to maybe play soprano at that time?

No. They had some — at that time they had some old sopranos, people was giving sopranos away because nobody was playing them. And I didn’t even think about playing, because I started out on a C melody. So that’s the first thing. But they had old sopranos and stuff around and people weren’t, you know nobody was interested in them.
They were out of favor at that time.
That’s right. Bechet was probably the only one playing. And when I came up I didn’t come up listening to Bechet, I skipped that generation. I came up listening to Bird.
You came up listening to Bird.
I came up listening to Bird, yeah.
I mean all of that was there but when I heard Bird I knew that was the real thing.
